app_documentation:
UniStudy is a comprehensive university student study platform designed to facilitate collaborative learning and knowledge sharing among students. The platform serves as a centralized hub where students can upload, browse, and download study notes shared by their peers, while also enabling them to form and participate in subject-specific study groups for collaborative learning. The application addresses the common challenge students face in accessing quality study materials and finding study partners by creating a community-driven ecosystem where academic resources and peer connections are readily available.

The platform's main features include secure user registration and authentication using university email addresses, a robust study notes sharing system with search and filtering capabilities, study group formation and management tools, real-time group communication through messaging and announcements, and a comprehensive rating and review system to help students identify high-quality content. Built on a modern technology stack including React for the frontend, Node.js and Express for the backend, PostgreSQL for data management, JWT for authentication, and AWS S3 for scalable file storage, UniStudy provides a responsive mobile-first experience that works seamlessly across web and mobile devices.

The intended users are university students who need efficient ways to access study materials, collaborate with peers, and enhance their learning experience. The platform supports three user roles: Students who can upload notes and participate in groups, Group Admins who have special permissions to manage study groups and post announcements, and Platform Administrators who oversee the entire system. With features like subject-based categorization, download tracking, member activity indicators, and personalized dashboards, UniStudy empowers students to take control of their academic success through community-driven collaboration and resource sharing.

The application's design prioritizes usability with a clean visual hierarchy, intuitive navigation through bottom tabs, and card-based layouts that make content discovery effortless. The color scheme balances academic professionalism with approachability, using primary blue tones complemented by secondary purple accents. Key user flows guide students from registration through note discovery, group participation, and profile management, ensuring that all core functionalities are accessible within a few taps. The platform's architecture supports scalability and future enhancements while maintaining performance and security standards essential for educational applications.

glossary.Study Notes: Digital academic materials (PDFs, documents) uploaded by students to share with peers, containing lecture summaries, course materials, or study guides that can be searched, downloaded, and reviewed by other platform users.
glossary.Study Group: A collaborative learning space within the platform where students with shared academic interests can communicate, share resources, and coordinate study activities around specific subjects or topics, managed by a designated Group Admin.
glossary.Group Admin: A user role with elevated permissions within a study group who can post announcements, manage group settings, and moderate group activities, typically the student who created the group.
glossary.Rating and Review System: A feature allowing students to evaluate shared study notes on a 1-5 star scale and provide written feedback, helping the community identify high-quality materials and improving content discoverability.
glossary.JWT Authentication: JSON Web Token-based security mechanism used to verify user identity and maintain secure sessions across the platform, ensuring that only verified university students can access protected features.
glossary.AWS S3: Amazon Web Services Simple Storage Service used as the scalable cloud storage solution for hosting uploaded study note files, providing reliable and secure file storage with URL-based access.
